(i) the dynamics of a system with many degrees of freedom can be reduced to a small number of variables, (ii) this reduction can be done in a systematic way and is valid in the limit of large drift and weak noise, (iii) this reduction is useful for the description of biological and chemical systems, (iv) the method is applicable to a broad range of systems with a wide range of noise statistics, (v) the method can also be used in the infinite dimensional setting

(i) we derive an explicit and general formula for a reduced dimension description of stochastic dynamical systems driven by small noise, that is exact in this limit, (ii) the formula can be applied to systems with infinite dimensional state space, and (iii) it can also be applied to processes with non-Gaussian noise.

(a) the dimension of the effective dynamics of a system of many interacting agents can often be much lower than that of the full system; and (b) this dimension reduction can be achieved by a simple procedure, based on a linear projection of the full system, that can be carried out in a straightforward and systematic manner for many classes of stochastic systems.
